chapter: Tiny Bradshaw, Teddy Hill and Europe
title: Teddy Hill as leader: regular rehearsals, but no knack like Chick's
summary: Hill was a mediocre tenor player who had a good stomp-down band including Chu Berry and Dicky Wells, but unlike Webb he didn't surround himself with the best talent.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: All right. So -- okay, anything else before we leave Teddy Hill?

Well, Teddy Hill was -- he was a most peculiar musician in that he wasn't a very good saxophone player. He had worked earlier with Lou Russell's band. He was the tenor player in Lou Russell's band, and then when he had this band he -- he had a good band up at the Savoy. At one time he
had Chu Berry, Dickie Wells and Bill Dillard. A very good stomp down band. One thing about him, he had rehearsals regularly, you know. Sort of a regular thing, and he'd buy arrangements, you know.
I guess he had a good ear for hiring the right --
Yeah, well, I suppose so, yeah. But not as much as Chick did.

Chick just had this natural born knack of putting it together. Putting it together. You know, he could really put it together, which most band leaders don't have. And Teddy Hill, he didn't really have that, the musicians, you know. But he was a person -- he thought that -- he was just the opposite of a man who -- if you have an organization, whatever it be, a musical organization or whatever, and you have to have people -- you're supposed to surround yourself with the best talent you can get. You know, if you had a supermarket you'd want the best help. But Teddy wasn't that way. He wouldn't want anyone to outshine him. And he wasn't a person who could produce that much. He wasn't a good saxophone player at all. For instance, I mean he couldn't stand up and feature himself on the saxophone. He couldn't do that. He was just a mediocre, I'd say.
